title: Ops Credit Sprint & Commitment Flex Playbook for Private/VPC and On‑Prem
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Objective: Define and validate a modular pricing/packaging playbook for Private/VPC and on‑prem customers that combines an anchored license fee with optional operational credit bundles and flexible upgrade cadences. The playbook should make enterprise negotiations faster, reduce legal back-and-forth on entitlements, and enable predictable engineering capacity planning. Scope: 1) Four packaging archetypes (Entry, Stabilize, Performance, Enterprise) each with a license anchor and optional Ops Credit bundles (monthly or burstable). 2) Support tier definitions (Standard / Priority / Critical) with response SLAs, included advisory hours, and security questionnaire readiness levels. 3) Upgrade cadence options (Quarterly scheduled, Monthly critical-only, Emergency hotfix window) and associated maintenance credits. 4) A standard SOW template and a mapped security questionnaire checklist for Sales & Legal to accelerate risk reviews. Success metrics: a) Reduce average contract negotiation time for Private deals from 28 days to <=14 days; b) Increase conversion on Sales-executed pilots by 12% when Ops Credits are offered; c) <10% of deals require a bespoke SLA amendment. Out of scope: deep legal pricing modeling, per-customer cost analysis (handled by finance), and non-Redwood-managed appliance packaging. Stakeholders: Sales (uptake), Legal (contracts), Finance (revenue modeling), Solutions Eng (pilot validation), Security (questionnaire mapping), Engineering (upgrade cadence feasibility).
acceptance_criteria: Four package archetypes documented with price anchors and included units
Ops Credit SKU matrix (monthly, burst, one-time) with pricing guidance
Support tiers defined with response time, escalation path, and included advisory hours
Upgrade cadence options documented and mapped to expected engineering windows and penalty thresholds
Security questionnaire mapping completed for each package and labelled with required controls
SOW & pricing sheet templates drafted and approved by Legal and Finance
Pilot plan defined with KPIs and success gates for two enterprise customers
comments: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: Alignment call with Sales and Solutions Eng. Agreed to prioritize a seatless and seat-based anchor for Entry tier; Sales asked for a simple one-page pricing summary for initial outreach. Action: draft pricing anchors by 2026-03-03 (Luca).

2026-03-01 - Legal review preview: Legal (M. Patel) flagged that 'upgrade cadence' language must include maintenance notification windows and rollback guarantees. Scheduling follow-up with Legal on 2026-03-05.

2026-03-04 - Finance feedback (J. Rivera): suggested two anchor styles: (A) fixed annual license + ops credits, (B) lower fixed license + consumption-aligned ops credits. We will model expected ARR ranges against both by 2026-03-11.

2026-03-06 - Solutions Eng notes: engineering capacity for monthly upgrade cadence requires a dedicated fast-path on our private upgrade runner; ENG dependency created. Added engineering feasibility requirement to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-09 - Security runbook draft uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Private+Packaging+Security+Checklist (internal). Security asked for 3 control tiers mapping to package archetypes.

2026-03-11 - Draft pricing sheet circulated to sales champions and 2 AE pilots. Early feedback: AEs prefer a 'credits per seat-equivalent' line to present to infra teams. Action: include alternate presentation slide by 2026-03-13.

2026-03-12 - PM review: consolidated playbook with initial SOW template (drive link) and checklist for Security Questionnaire. Next step: schedule cross-functional review on 2026-03-16 and prepare two pilot proposals (customer A: fintech, customer B: healthcare).
